payload.friction_text: HomeBase kit upgrade 3.5.0 → 3.8.0 (run from HomeBase) shipped an INCOMPLETE kit/scripts set: 121 of the runtime scripts installed, but 6 of them imported sibling modules that were NOT copied into the adopter — cwos-pulse.js→./cwos-value-ratio, cwos-verify.js→./cwos-runtime-dispatch-audit + ./cwos-readpath-lint, cwos-adopt-install.js + cwos-migrate.js→./lib/cwos-kit-dirs + ./lib/cwos-bundle-validate, cwos-engine-complete.js→./lib/cwos-skill-telemetry. Result: /pulse, /verify, /adopt-install, /migrate, /engine-complete crash on load (unresolvable import). Caught by npm run preflight:staged (deploy CI gate) BEFORE commit — a commit would have broken CI + shipped non-functional commands. This is a HomeBase distribution-MANIFEST bug: the adopter copy-set omits transitive runtime deps of the scripts it does copy. Affects any repo adopted/upgraded via the same MANIFEST — fleet-level.
payload.workaround: Computed the transitive missing-dep closure (exactly 6 files; they pull in nothing further) and copied them verbatim from HomeBase kit/scripts/ into this repo to complete the dependency graph. Re-ran preflight (✓ 130 files resolve) + smoke-confirmed cwos-pulse + cwos-verify load. UPSTREAM FIX NEEDED at HomeBase: add cwos-value-ratio.js, cwos-runtime-dispatch-audit.js, cwos-readpath-lint.js, lib/cwos-kit-dirs.js, lib/cwos-bundle-validate.js, lib/cwos-skill-telemetry.js to the adopter copy-set in kit/MANIFEST.yaml (or whatever drives cwos-adopt-install's file selection) so future adopts/upgrades ship them.

payload.friction_text: cwos-next.js done never stamps completed_at / completion_commit on queue items created from the standard ticket template. The patch logic guards on field PRESENCE (`if (!/^completed_at:/m.test(patched))`) but the template pre-declares `completed_at: null` and `completion_commit: null`, so the guard sees the field, skips the write, and the null survives closure. Measured across this repo's queue: 42 of 69 done items carry completed_at:null; the 27 stamped ones predate the template or were hand-fixed. Closure is still fully recoverable — the item_closed event carries the timestamp and state/queue.json materializes correctly — so this is a provenance gap in the editable surface, not lost data. Also affects closed_by_event only incidentally (that one appends unconditionally). Noticed while closing WS-269.
payload.workaround: None applied — out of scope for WS-269 (the sprint in flight) and non-blocking. Kit fix: change the three guards from presence to value checks (treat `null`/empty as unstamped) and patch in place rather than inserting, e.g. replace `^completed_at:.*$` when the captured value is null. Worth a backfill pass over the 42 stale items at the same time.

payload.friction_text: cwos-verify.js reports kit-SOURCE-only invariants as FAIL in an adopter repo that has no kit/ source tree, rather than N/A. Measured this run: 17 FAILs, of which 11 are structurally inapplicable here - INV-002 (engines/INDEX.md not found), INV-008 (fleet/registry.yaml not found), INV-009 (docs/adrs/INDEX.md), INV-010 (docs/guides/user-guide.md), INV-013, INV-014 (registry template), INV-024 + INV-049 + INV-056 (kit/MANIFEST.yaml / kit/commands/ not found), INV-059, INV-060 (engines/standard/*). Several sibling invariants in the same run DO handle this correctly and report PASS with an explicit N/A reason (INV-064 'no kit/MANIFEST.yaml - N/A (not a kit source repo)', INV-063, INV-065), so the convention exists and these checks simply predate or missed it. Consequence is signal dilution, not breakage: a real regression has to be picked out of a standing wall of 17 red lines, which is exactly the condition under which people stop reading the output.
payload.workaround: None applied - out of scope for an ad-hoc bug-fix session, and non-blocking. Verified by inspection that none of the 17 touch view code, so the session's own changes are clean. Kit fix: make the missing-artifact branch of these 11 checks emit PASS/N-A with a reason (the INV-064 pattern) instead of FAIL when the repo is not a kit source repo.

payload.feedback_text: Verify ticket premise against current code DURING /next composition, before approval — not mid-execution
payload.detail: SPR-095's two anchors were authored by a Gate-2 blind-spot audit and both had premises that didn't match the code: WS-206 assumed LSW line nodes store an asserted-equity number to validate against (none exists — equity is prose-only), forcing a mid-sprint reframe + an extra founder decision; WS-205 risked duplicating existing equity infra (computeComboEquityDistribution). The approval option also said "~68 nodes" when only 5 were parity-eligible. This is the SAME pattern flagged one sprint earlier (SPR-094: WS-204 was a duplicate of pre-existing work) — now a confirmed RECURRING failure mode of audit-authored tickets. Fix: /next composition should spend ~2 min checking each anchor's core assumption (does the data structure exist? is the work already done? what's the real scope/count?) against the codebase BEFORE presenting for approval, so reframes/scope-corrections happen upfront in one accurate proposal instead of as mid-flight interruptions.

payload.feedback_text: /next resume-check only looks for status:active — misses approved-but-unexecuted sprints
payload.detail: SPR-095 was status:approved with items_done:0 (a prior session composed + got it approved, then stopped before executing). /next Step 1 only scans for status:active, so a freshly-approved-but-unstarted sprint is invisible to the resume path and a new /next would stack a second sprint on top, orphaning the approved work. Caught only by luck (reading a sprint file for schema reference). Fix: Step 1 resume-check should also surface sprints where status==approved AND completed_at==null (especially items_done<item_count) and offer to resume them.

payload.feedback_text: queue-index drift + soft-block flag absent from index make /next ranking unreliable
payload.detail: queue-index.yaml disagreed with the WS-*.yaml files: WS-205/206 showed status:backlog in the index but were claimed in their files; WS-185 showed backlog but was done. Separately, the index summary does NOT carry blocked_by_note, so soft-blocked items (the P=22 monetization cluster, WS-191, WS-047, WS-092) surfaced at full priority in the first-pass ranking until each WS file was opened. Both stem from the absent cwos-reconcile.js (no automated index rebuild) — see fr-002/fr-011. Fix: install the reconcile suite, OR mirror blocked_by_note into the index, OR have /next read candidate WS files before ranking (slower but correct).
